C-EXT-TRUST-COHERENCE.Summary: Make the extension trust lifecycle coherent end to end: the incoming data routes (/ext/text-insert, /ext/context, /ext/apply) get the same post-authentication disable fence the /stream/* routes already have; a disable in flight cancels a pending context read instead of serving it; a disable whose credential revocation failed can no longer be silently undone by the retry-enable path — re-arming requires an explicit successful revocation retry or a fresh pairing, and the gallery retry button keeps sending Disable; and a rebind whose manifest has grown incoming rights shows them in the pairing dialog before any grant is overwritten, with the dialog never displaying a caller-reported name that contradicts the registered manifest.
C-EXT-TRUST-COHERENCE.Problem: Verified against the current worktree (branch spec/ext-trust-coherence, base 689df8aa); the wave-2 scout findings 5, 7, 8 and 12 share one cause — the disable fencing introduced by C-SEC-STREAM-AUTH (auth under a stale-proof, then an authorization_epoch re-check under stream_gate, live_server.rs:1176-1183) covers only /stream/*, while the incoming data routes and the key/grant lifecycle drift out of sync with the fact of revocation. (1) In-flight data routes skip the enabled fence: handle_text_insert authenticates (live_server.rs:1547) and emits mt::text::op (1568) with no re-check; handle_ext_apply authenticates (1694), passes the C-SEC-EDIT-TARGETING binding fence and emits the whole batch (1745-1796) answering applied:true (1804-1810) with no re-check. The fence window is real: authenticate_incoming performs keyring I/O inside spawn_blocking (live_server.rs:698-705), and mt_ext_disable flips the registry state under the same stream_gate the stream handlers hold (mod.rs:160-171, registry.rs:133-150 bumps authorization_epoch), so a request that passed authentication before the disable still emits content after it; the renderer gate checks only the document binding, never enabled state (editor.vue:3388-3391). (2) /ext/context is fenced even less: one authentication (1598), then the pending entry (1614-1617), the renderer request, and a 5 s wait (1635) during which a disable touches nothing — mt_ext_disable clears no pending entry (mod.rs:160-171) — and the renderer answers unconditionally (editor.vue:3580-3625, handleExtContextRequest has no enabled check); the response is served and recorded into EXT_DOCUMENT_BINDINGS (1642-1651) for an extension that is disabled by the time it arrives. (3) The revoke-retry loop re-arms the surviving key: after ext_disable_revoke_failed (mod.rs:178-181) the registry flag is already false (registry.disable ran at 163) while the secret survives, and the grant revocation is skipped entirely (the failure returns before the grant block at 182-196); the gallery then chooses the action from the stale flag — index.vue:178 `const action = ext.enabled ? 'mt_ext_disable' : 'mt_ext_enable'` — so the owner's retry sends mt_ext_enable, and mt_ext_enable re-keys nothing when a secret exists (mod.rs:102-107) and passes the #298 coverage gate because the stored grant is still in place: the pre-disable credential with its pre-disable grant goes live again, exactly the state the failed disable said it could not establish. (4) A rebind overwrites the grant without showing it: the approved-grant capture (live_server.rs:889-909) intersects the CURRENT manifest into the stored grant on every approved pair including a rebind, while the rebind dialog states the opposite — its doc comment and text say "a rebind changes no grant set — the same manifest stays in force" (live_server.rs:746-759) — so a manifest grown between pairings gains incoming rights at rebind time with no dialog line, bypassing the enable-side growth gate of C-SEC-EXT-GRANT-BOUND (mod.rs:115-143) because the rebind rewrites the grant first; the same overwrite silently narrows the grant when the manifest shrank. (5) The dialogs trust the caller-reported identity: the descriptions are built from PairRequest.extension_name/extension_id (live_server.rs:851-855, 175-183) and no comparison against the registered manifest's name exists — the grant lines are manifest-derived (peek_manifest, 796-801), but the human decides on a name the requesting process invented. Finding 9 (honest retoken) is already closed by C-SEC-PAIR-REBIND and #298 (rebind_refused_when_new_key_fails_verification tests.rs:1644, pair_keychain_read_error_is_a_distinct_refusal 1662); this change must compose with it, not weaken it.
C-EXT-TRUST-COHERENCE.Relationship: Lineage, all landed: C-SEC-STREAM-AUTH built the disable-fencing pattern this change extends to the data routes (stream_gate ordering, authorization_epoch invalidation on register/enable/disable, the "extension is not enabled" refusal voice) — its semantics and its suite (stream_disabled_owner_is_fenced_even_when_keyring_delete_fails tests.rs:1877, stream_foreign_owner_cannot_disclose_or_replace_session 1890, stream_authentication_cannot_cross_disable_or_session_replacement 1924, stream_events_keep_ordered_identity_and_disable_only_closes_its_owner 1968) are untouched and keep passing. C-SEC-EXT-GRANT-BOUND (#298) owns the stored grant, the enable coverage gate and the honest replace — this change adds no capability name, does not move the gate's semantics, and pins that its regressions keep passing unchanged in meaning: pairing_persists_the_captured_grant (tests.rs:1513), grow_after_pairing_enable_is_refused_to_reapproval (1545), legacy_credential_without_grant_fails_closed (1593), stream_requires_stored_stream_document_grant (1609), rebind_refused_when_new_key_fails_verification (1644), pair_keychain_read_error_is_a_distinct_refusal (1662). C-SEC-PAIR-REBIND owns the constant-time prior-secret rebind gate and the old-key-death proof — untouched; the growth dialog composes on top of an already-proven rebind. C-SEC-EDIT-TARGETING owns the binding fence — untouched; the enabled fence precedes it and never answers applied:true on refusal. The repository locale canon (the ten-locale precedent of C-10/C-12/C-32/C-56, e.g. extensions.disableFailed) applies: every new gallery-visible user string ships in all ten locale files. Coordination with the parallel C-EXT-EDIT-PROOF (#321, in review): it reworks the same handlers (the /ext/text-insert honest refusal, the /ext/apply ack channel with a dedup short-circuit and validation-before-emit, invoke retry policy) and this change lands on top of it. The composed per-route order is pinned here: capability authentication (authenticate_incoming) — enabled fence (this change) — #321's dedup short-circuit — binding fence — #321's op validation — emit/ack. A replay from a disabled extension is refused by the fence, never served a recorded verdict, so #321's "dedup runs after authentication and before the fence" statement is read against its binding fence and is superseded in ordering by this fence; #321's read-only-main.rs constraint is preserved because the pending_context value type gains the extension id inside live_server.rs while the LiveServerState literal (src-tauri/src/main.rs:823-828) is textually unchanged; #321's two moved text-insert pins are not moved further — on the merged tree the /ext/text-insert fence collapses into the route's auth-first refusal ordering and the plan says so. This bundle is one of four triaged from the 2026-11-22 wave-2 scout (B2; neighboring bundles B1 EDIT-PROOF, B3 GALLERY-STATE, B4 DELIVERY-HONESTY are explicitly non-goals here) and closes the trust half of the wave-2 acceptance criterion: a refused save or a revocation leaves the rights and the interface in a consistent state.

Goals.Goal: The incoming data routes carry the disable fence. authenticate_incoming returns the authorization_epoch snapshot beside the resolved extension id, and each data handler re-checks it under stream_gate exactly like the stream handlers' identity.is_enabled (the StreamIdentity precedent, live_server.rs:553-560): handle_text_insert and handle_ext_apply take stream_gate after authentication, refuse with 401 and the file's plain "extension is not enabled" body — the same voice as the stream fence at live_server.rs:1179 — plus a distinct BLOCK_ log, when the epoch no longer matches, and hold the gate across the in-memory pre-emit section (epoch re-check, binding lookup, emit loop). The gate is never held across a bounded renderer wait (the context round trip, #321's apply ack budget), across keyring I/O, or in any order other than today's stream_gate before session. A fenced request emits nothing and never answers ok:true or applied:true; the refusal is immediate, never a timeout.

A disable cancels the context reads it owns. The pending context entry carries its extension id; mt_ext_disable — already inside the stream_gate fence (mod.rs:160-171) — drains the disabled extension's pending entries, so the waiting handler wakes immediately instead of serving a response after the fact: it answers 401 with the fence voice and a distinct log when the enabled re-check shows the cancellation, keeps the existing channel-closed 500 for a renderer that dropped its entry, discards any late mt::ext::context_response for a drained entry (the listener at live_server.rs:1954-1969 already drops missing entries), and records nothing into EXT_DOCUMENT_BINDINGS. A disable whose drain wins the race never resolves the wait with content for that extension (a response that legitimately overtook the drain was produced while the extension was still enabled and is bounded by the same fence ordering); the plan documents the composed epoch re-check if it strengthens this further. The renderer stays untouched: the server-side cancellation is the authoritative fence.

A failed revocation stays failed until proven otherwise. On ext_disable_revoke_failed, mt_ext_disable records a persistent revoke-pending marker beside the credential (an auth.rs record keyed like the grant record, a constant value, no secret material — the auth.rs two-records-per-id precedent at auth.rs:179-232); mt_ext_enable refuses with a distinct machine code (ext_enable_revoke_pending, with a distinct logged state when the marker itself is unreadable) while the marker stands, so the surviving secret cannot be silently re-armed; the marker clears only on proof — a successful disable (strict persistent and memory absence, the existing condition at mod.rs:172-181) or a successful pairing (a rebind's honest-replace proof already establishes the prior record dead). The gallery's retry stays Disable: the toggle action is chosen from the operation outcome, not only the refetched flag — after a failed disable the retry sends mt_ext_disable again, the flag clears on a successful disable or when the list shows the extension enabled again, and the new enable-refusal code surfaces as an explicit instruction (a new extensions-namespace key in all ten locales). A disable that already succeeded, and the disable-pair-enable trust reset of #298 (fresh_pairing_restores_access, tests.rs:1435), keep working exactly as today.

A rebind that would grow the grant asks first. Before the approval decision, handle_pair classifies the rebind grant change against the stored grant (a pure helper: growth listing the added names, equality, narrowing; an unreadable stored grant is a distinct logged 500 refusal that pairs nothing). Growth selects the full grant dialog: it keeps the key-replacement statement and enumerates every added capability with its grant phrase vocabulary (the pairing_grant_description lines), so approval is informed and denial refuses the rebind with the prior key fully valid; equality and narrowing keep the quiet dialog, whose text is made honest — it states no grant change only when none occurs, and states the narrowing when the manifest shrank, instead of today's unconditional "a rebind changes no grant set" (live_server.rs:746-759). The stored grant after any approved pair remains exactly the presented capture: the current manifest's incoming subset in RouteCapability::all() order (#298's capture rule). A legacy credential with no stored grant being rebound classifies as growth and is shown in full before any grant is captured for it.

The pairing dialogs display the registered name. For a registered id the dialog text uses the registered manifest's name; a caller-reported extension_name that differs from it never reaches the user and is a distinct logged state (a pure decision helper beside pairing_grant_description, pinned like pairing_grant_description_names_only_declared_capabilities at tests.rs:1396). An unregistered id keeps the reported name — there is nothing to compare against — and the prior-secret rebind gate is unchanged.

Honest retoken (scout key 9) is regression-insured, not reworked: the growth-approval path composes with the old-key-death proof — an approved growth rebind still answers paired:true only after the prior token verifiably no longer validates (the live_server.rs:929-978 proof, unchanged) — and the #298/C-SEC-PAIR-REBIND pins named in Relationship keep their assertions and statuses.

Constraints.Constraint: Exact ObservedWriteScope, enumerated by reading the current tree:

Read-only anchors: src-tauri/src/main.rs (the LiveServerState literal at main.rs:823-828 stays untouched — the pending_context value type gains the extension id inside live_server.rs while the literal expression is unchanged); registry.rs (authorization_epoch, peek_manifest, get_manifest, get_enabled and the stream_gate are consumed as-is — the revoke-pending marker deliberately lives in auth.rs so re-discovery's state-overwriting register, registry.rs:91-110, cannot clear it); live_bridge.rs, manifest.rs, discovery.rs, text_ops.rs, invoke.rs (B1/B3/B4 territory); editor.vue is entirely outside the write scope — the context fence is server-side only, which also keeps this change out of the EXT_TEXT_OPS block #321 is reworking.

#321 coordination is anchor-semantic, not line-numeric: the fence anchors are "immediately after the authenticate_incoming call in each data handler, before any dedup, fence, validation or emit", and the plan re-anchors on the merged tree. The composed route order pinned in Relationship is the target state regardless of merge order; if #321 lands after this change, the plan applies the same composition from the other side. #321's response-shape work on /ext/apply is untouched here — this change adds no wire fields and no new response shapes; its externally visible additions are refusal statuses and bodies on newly fenced paths and one new gallery error code.

Lock and budget discipline: stream_gate is held only across in-memory work (epoch re-check, binding lookup, synchronous emit leg, pending registration and drain); no keyring I/O and no bounded renderer wait happens under it, and the lock order stays stream_gate, then session, then the pending-context map (a leaf std Mutex with no inverse-order path). The context handler releases the gate before its 5 s wait; cancellation covers that wait by draining the pending entry, not by holding the gate.

Security hygiene unchanged: no log line, error body, dialog or marker record carries secret material (the marker is a constant; grants hold capability names only; comparisons stay constant time); the disable order of C-SEC-STREAM-AUTH/#298 — fence and deactivate under stream_gate, strict revocation, best-effort grant revocation — keeps its sequence and its success condition, and the marker is written on the existing failure branch without moving either; the loopback-only binding and Bearer model are unchanged; the prior-secret rebind gate and the old-key-death proof are unchanged.

i18n per the repository ten-locale canon (C-10/C-12/C-32/C-56 precedent): exactly one new gallery-visible instruction (the revoke-pending/retry state) is added under the extensions namespace in all ten static/locales/*.json files, and the existing disableFailed text keeps its meaning; the pairing dialogs stay native-dialog English in live_server.rs, which is their current voice, so their rewording triggers no locale work.

Predecessor suites keep meaning with zero moved pins: the disable-revocation suite (tests.rs:1322, 1340, 1351), the #298 grant/rebind pins (1513, 1545, 1593, 1609, 1644, 1662, plus the description pin 1396), the binding matrix (1159-1231), the stream security suite (1877-1989) and the incoming-route refusal pins (1056-1150) pass unchanged — no existing test asserts the failed-disable enable behavior or the post-failure gallery action, so this change moves no existing pin; the fixture gains the marker backend injection mechanically inside incoming_fixture_with_grant (tests.rs:961-1035) without changing any call site.

Repository artifacts stay English and the GRACE surface is synchronized (module contracts and CHANGE_SUMMARY entries of live_server.rs, auth.rs, mod.rs, tests.rs, index.vue; module maps; graph; verification); no version change, release, publication or deploy is authorized by this specification.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No edit-pipeline work (scout keys 1, 2, 3, 11, 17, 19 — bundle B1, C-EXT-EDIT-PROOF #321): no ack channel, no apply idempotency or dedup design, no dead-route refusal decision, no invoke retry or Retry-After change, no /stream/* budget change.

No gallery-state work (scout keys 4, 13, 14, 15, 16 — bundle B3): re-discovery still resets enabled in register, no discovery sequencing, scan-error surfacing or list-freshness work; the retry-sync here covers only the failed-disable outcome, not stale-list flip generally.
No delivery-honesty work (scout keys 18, 20, 10 — bundle B4): no endpoint publication retry, no doc_open ack channel, no InvokeError body sanitization.
No renderer-side enabled check in editor.vue's context responder — the server-side drain and the fence make it redundant; editor.vue, textOps.js and their suites are untouched.

No persistence redesign: the enabled flag and the registry stay process-local as today; the revoke-pending marker is the single added credential-lifecycle record, and no migration is planned — an id that never had a failed revocation has no marker and behaves exactly as today, including the enable-mint path of #298.

No new capability names, no manifest schema change, no pairing UX surface beyond the existing single native dialog (the growth variant rewords the same dialog), no change to the enable coverage gate's semantics, and no per-operation or time-limited credentials.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Failing-first in-flight fence on /ext/apply: with the credential read paused inside authenticate_incoming (the DummyCredential read_pause mechanism, tests.rs:1250-1262, the stream_authentication_cannot_cross_disable pattern at 1924), a disable completing during the paused authentication makes the resumed apply answer 401 with the "extension is not enabled" body and a distinct logged state, with zero mt::text::op events and no EXT_DOCUMENT_BINDINGS mutation — today the same interleaving answers 200 applied:true and emits the batch (live_server.rs:1694-1810), so the assertion is red before the fix. The same criterion holds for a disable completing anywhere between authentication and the emit leg.

Failing-first in-flight fence on /ext/text-insert: the identical paused-authentication disable leg answers an explicit non-2xx refusal with zero events — today it answers 200 {"ok": true} with one emitted event (live_server.rs:1547-1586). On the tree merged with #321 the route already refuses; the pin then composes with that refusal (the disabled leg never depends on emit ordering and never reports success), and the plan documents the exact composed status.

Failing-first context cancellation: a /ext/context whose extension is disabled while the request is pending (the read_pause leg, or a disable between the fence and the response) wakes immediately with 401 and the fence voice, serves no markdown, records no binding — a follow-up apply echoing the binding the renderer would have handed answers 409, proving nothing was recorded — and a late mt::ext::context_response for the drained entry is discarded; today the response is served and recorded (live_server.rs:1635-1657), so every leg is red before the fix. A disable between authentication and the emit leg refuses at the fence with zero renderer traffic.

Failing-first enable gate: after ext_disable_revoke_failed (the fail_delete pattern of disable_surfaces_revoke_failure, tests.rs:1340), mt_ext_enable returns Err("ext_enable_revoke_pending"), leaves the registry disabled, re-keys nothing and leaves the surviving credential inert; a subsequent successful disable clears the state and the disable-pair-enable flow then works exactly as pinned by fresh_pairing_restores_access (tests.rs:1435); a successful rebind after the failed disable also clears it — today mt_ext_enable succeeds and re-arms the pre-disable credential with its pre-disable grant (mod.rs:102-149), so the refusal is red before the fix. An unreadable marker is a distinct logged refusal that enables nothing.

Failing-first gallery retry sync: after a toggle whose mt_ext_disable rejects with 'ext_disable_revoke_failed', the next toggle on the same card sends mt_ext_disable again — today it sends mt_ext_enable because the action is chosen from the refetched enabled:false flag (index.vue:178), so the new assertion is red before the fix; the pending state clears after a successful disable and when the list shows the extension enabled; and the ext_enable_revoke_pending refusal surfaces the new instruction text from the ten-locale key, in the manner of the existing re-approval mapping test (index.test.js:152-165), which keeps passing.

Failing-first rebind grant honesty: the pure change-classification helper distinguishes growth (added names), equality and narrowing from the stored grant; the growth rebind dialog text names every added capability's grant phrase plus the key-replacement statement, the equality text claims no grant change, the narrowing text states it — today the single unconditional "a rebind changes no grant set" text (live_server.rs:746-759) serves all three while the capture overwrites the grant from the current manifest (889-909), so the pins are red before the fix. Harness-side, an approved growth rebind stores the presented capture including the added name, a denied growth rebind leaves the prior grant and prior key fully valid, and a legacy credential with no stored grant classifies as growth and is shown in full before any capture.

Failing-first dialog name trust: the pure name-decision helper yields the registered manifest's name for a registered id and a distinct mismatch state when the caller-reported name differs — today no comparison exists (live_server.rs:851-855), so the pin is red before the fix; the mismatch state is logged and the reported name is never displayed; an unregistered id keeps the reported name.

Failing-first retoken composition (key 9 insurance): an approved growth rebind answers paired:true only after the prior-token-death proof — the proof branches and their distinct refusals (live_server.rs:929-978, pinned by rebind_refused_when_new_key_fails_verification tests.rs:1644 and pair_keychain_read_error_is_a_distinct_refusal 1662) are exercised unchanged on the growth path; and every predecessor suite named in Constraints passes with unchanged assertions after the fix, with no moved pins anywhere in this change.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Each named failing-first behavior — the in-flight apply and insert fence refusals (401 voice, zero events, no binding mutation), the context cancellation (immediate wake, no content, no binding record, late response discarded), the revoke-pending enable refusal and its two proof paths for clearing, the gallery retry sending Disable again plus the new instruction surfacing, the rebind growth/equality/narrowing dialog pins, the dialog name-trust pin, and the retoken composition on the growth path — fails before the fix and passes after it; the disable-revocation, grant-bound, rebind, stream-security, binding-matrix and incoming-refusal suites pass with unchanged assertions (no moved pins); the extensionGallery vitest suite stays green with the new retry-sync and mapping pins. Before archiving: grace lint --path . --change C-EXT-TRUST-COHERENCE --assertions final --run-commands, then grace lint --path . --assertions current and grace status --path . --with modules --json.

Assumptions.Assumption: The revoke-pending marker persists through the credential store (keyring record with memory mirror and verify-through-read, the store_grant discipline at auth.rs:213-232) so the coherence survives an application restart between the failed disable and the retry; a marker write failing alongside the revocation failure is a distinct logged residual (a backend that cannot delete usually cannot write) and is documented, not handled, in this change.

The growth dialog is the same single native rfd dialog with extended text — no new UI surface; in test builds the dialog arm is compiled out (the existing cfg pattern at live_server.rs:841-876), so dialog-wording behavior is pinned through the pure helpers and the harness-approved path, exactly how pairing_grant_description is pinned today (tests.rs:1396).

Mark's extension gallery surfaces backend refusal codes as instruction text; the pairing dialogs remain native-dialog English (their current voice), so the repository ten-locale canon (C-10/C-12/C-32/C-56 precedent) applies only to the one new gallery string here.

#321 (C-EXT-EDIT-PROOF) merges before this change is implemented; if the order reverses, the plan reconciles the anchors on whichever tree is current, with the composed ordering in Relationship as the invariant. This draft's approval approves neither an unwritten plan nor apply/archive, lane departure or release; the marker key name, the refusal reason strings, the new i18n key name and log-marker names are plan-level constants within the bounds pinned here.

AffectedAreas stays M-045-only, following the C-SEC-EXT-GRANT-BOUND precedent (extensionGallery/index.vue in scope, M-011 not claimed): editor.vue and the M-011 editor surface are untouched by this change by design.
